source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Add a new user account by
    - IPMI command -
         Send command: ipmitool user set name <User ID> <Username>
         Send command: ipmitool user set password <User ID> (<Password>)
         Send command: ipmitool user enable <User ID>
         Send command: ipmitool user priv <User ID> <Privilege level> <Channel number>
         Send command: ipmitool channel setaccess 1 <user id> link=on privilege=4 ipmi=on
         Send command: ipmitool sol payload enable 1 <user id>
         (User ID: Use an user ID that has NOT been used. (Can use "ipmitool user list <Channel number>" to see "Empty user"))
2. Check user list.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. New user account should be added successfully.
2. New user account should be displayed correctly.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Create a user with operator-supplied ID/name/password using ipmitool set name/password/enable, then verify with user list; the source DeepSeek command hard-codes cipher 17 and exposes the password through -P.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Return full add output and the subsequent user list.
deepseek_columns.risk: Adding a BMC user is a security-sensitive write; use a scratch user ID, confirm values and remove it after test.

original_test_intent: Verify IPMI can create and enable a new BMC user in an unused slot, apply the intended privilege and access on the intended management channel, optionally enable the required SOL payload, and display the resulting account correctly.
original_method: After approving an unused disposable slot, exact username/password policy, target channel, least-privilege role and SOL scope, capture the complete account/channel baseline; perform each source write once using protected credential input; read back name, enabled state, privilege, channel access and SOL payload independently; perform bounded positive and negative authorization checks; then remove or restore only the scratch account and prove the baseline/recovery users remain intact.
manual_activity: An owner selects and approves the scratch slot, username/password policy, channel, least privilege, access flags, SOL scope, authentication matrix and cleanup. A human maintains independent recovery access and issues the formal verdict; the approved individual writes and readbacks may then be automated without physical work.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity and pinned ipmitool behavior
Unused disposable user ID proven across relevant channels
Protected/recovery account and independent access list
Username/password policy and protected secret mechanism
Authoritative management channel and slot mapping
Requested least-privilege role and access flags
SOL requirement and payload channel if applicable
Positive/negative authorization checks and cleanup/restore method
safety_requirements: Do not use a protected, occupied, root or recovery user ID; prove the immutable numeric slot and channel mapping before the first write.
Do not place either administrative or new-user passwords in `-P`, command text, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review records.
Do not assume channel 1, privilege 4 or SOL enablement. Resolve the source's conflicting placeholders and hard-coded values before execution.
Obtain explicit approval for the exact ordered writes. Execute each once, read back immediately and stop without automatic retry on an unexpected state.
Keep an independent local/admin recovery session and verify unrelated accounts, channel access and active sessions after every material step.
Do not clear SEL/security/audit logs. Preserve redacted audit evidence and stop on secret exposure, wrong slot/channel, excess privilege or recovery-access change.
Remove or restore only the scratch account with a vendor-supported method; verify complete per-channel baseline recovery and rotate any exposed test secret.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the target, disposable slot, channel/role/access/SOL matrix, protected credentials, recovery path and exact approved write sequence.
Capture complete per-channel account/access/SOL baseline without clearing logs.
After explicit approval, apply name, password, enable, privilege, channel access and optional SOL operations one at a time with immediate readback and no retry.
Perform bounded authentication and allowed/denied privilege checks that cannot damage the DUT.
Use the approved cleanup method, prove scratch removal/restoration and unrelated-account continuity, and return facts without a DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the source's `<Channel number>` versus channel 1 and `<Privilege level>` versus privilege 4 contradictions; approve whether SOL is mandatory.
Approve the disposable slot, least-privilege/access matrix, protected secret handling, bounded authorization tests and exact cleanup/recovery sequence.
Review complete before/after/audit evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The DeepSeek sequence covers name/password/enable but omits privilege, channel setaccess and SOL from the Master Procedure, exposes secrets with `-P`, fixes cipher 17 and does not reconcile the hard-coded channel/privilege conflict. Its final list alone cannot prove authentication or effective authorization.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the source operations but instantiate only engineer-approved slot/channel/least-privilege/access/SOL values, use protected password input, execute one write at a time and pair every write with authoritative readback plus bounded auth tests.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All six original IPMI operations, unused-ID note, user-list check, Script reference, Criteria, no Bundle and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review-layer gates do not overwrite Master.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create one disposable least-privilege account through the approved IPMI path with protected credentials, explicit per-channel access and opt-in SOL, verify inventory plus effective authorization, then remove/restore it under independent recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC IPMI user, channel-access and SOL implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, IPMI/vendor extension level and ipmitool version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor IPMI user-slot/channel/SOL semantics and Project account/security policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe slot discovery, protected credentials, conflict resolution, immediate readback, effective authorization, audit preservation and deterministic cleanup while retaining every source operation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Listing the account is only partial evidence; API/WebUI account creation is an override and does not prove the original IPMI command path unless equivalence is approved and uncovered coverage recorded.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved slot, secret policy, channel, role/access, SOL scope, auth matrix and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong slot, excess role or unintended SOL/channel access can create persistent unauthorized management access or impair recovery.

project_override_considerations: A vendor API or WebUI may replace the IPMI creation path only when the source method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, slot/channel/role/SOL coverage equivalence and remaining unverified IPMI behavior are recorded. Lack of a currently listed tool is not permanent BLOCKED.
expected_evidence: Approval, target/BMC/ipmitool identity, immutable scratch slot, protected-account list, channel/role/access/SOL matrix and redacted complete baseline
Per-operation result and audit event plus immediate authoritative readback for name, enabled state, privilege, channel access and optional SOL payload
Bounded login and allowed/denied authorization evidence proving effective least privilege without exposing secrets
Complete per-channel post-state showing no unrelated/protected-account, access or session change
Vendor-supported scratch cleanup/restoration, baseline/recovery confirmation, preserved logs and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within the preserved Master Procedure, privilege is first parameterized by `<Privilege level>` and `<Channel number>`, but the next access command hard-codes channel 1 and administrator privilege 4, and SOL also hard-codes channel 1. These competing instructions can create different effective access and require an engineer-approved authoritative matrix; neither value may be guessed.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The account-creation purpose and operations are identifiable. Channel, role, SOL and cleanup decisions are finite Project/engineer inputs, so review is complete and execution readiness is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its hybrid classification and scratch cleanup concept but rejects its exposed-password, incomplete and fixed-transport command as executable advice.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its classification and security lifecycle, while explicitly elevating the Master channel/privilege inconsistency to a preserved source conflict requiring decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic variable gating with exact slot/channel/role/SOL, recovery, readback, authorization and cleanup requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Separates read-only View evidence and the following Delete/disable semantics from this Add case's independent coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents credential leakage, wrong-slot writes and unintended administrator/SOL access while preserving the original IPMI creation coverage and exposing the Master command inconsistency for engineer resolution.
independent_technical_reasoning: An IPMI account is not proven by a successful name write or list row. Effective permission derives from the numeric slot, channel-specific privilege/access flags and optionally SOL payload state; the Master simultaneously parameterizes those values and hard-codes channel 1/admin privilege. Safe SIT coverage therefore needs an approved matrix, immediate readback, real least-privilege authorization checks and deterministic scratch cleanup under independent recovery.
